4982#########i#############################################################
4983# Tokenizer routines for looking ahead in input stream
4984#######################################################################
4985
4986sub peek_ahead_for_n_nonblank_pre_tokens {
4987
4988 # returns next n pretokens if they exist
4989 # returns undef's if hits eof without seeing any pretokens
4990 # USES GLOBAL VARIABLES: $tokenizer_self
4991 my $max_pretokens = shift;
4992 my $line;
4993 my $i = 0;
4994 my ( $rpre_tokens, $rmap, $rpre_types );
4995
4996 while ( $line = $tokenizer_self->{_line_buffer_object}->peek_ahead( $i++ ) )
4997 {
4998 $line =~ s/^\s*//; # trim leading blanks
4999 next if ( length($line) <= 0 ); # skip blank
5000 next if ( $line =~ /^#/ ); # skip comment
5001 ( $rpre_tokens, $rmap, $rpre_types ) =
5002 pre_tokenize( $line, $max_pretokens );
5003 last;
5004 }
5005 return ( $rpre_tokens, $rpre_types );
5006}
5007
5008# look ahead for next non-blank, non-comment line of code
5009sub peek_ahead_for_nonblank_token {
5010
5011 # USES GLOBAL VARIABLES: $tokenizer_self
5012 my ( $rtokens, $max_token_index ) = @_;
5013 my $line;
5014 my $i = 0;
5015
5016 while ( $line = $tokenizer_self->{_line_buffer_object}->peek_ahead( $i++ ) )
5017 {
5018 $line =~ s/^\s*//; # trim leading blanks
5019 next if ( length($line) <= 0 ); # skip blank
5020 next if ( $line =~ /^#/ ); # skip comment
5021 my ( $rtok, $rmap, $rtype ) =
5022 pre_tokenize( $line, 2 ); # only need 2 pre-tokens
5023 my $j = $max_token_index + 1;
5024
5025 foreach my $tok ( @{$rtok} ) {
5026 last if ( $tok =~ "\n" );
5027 $rtokens->[ ++$j ] = $tok;
5028 }
5029 last;
5030 }
5031 return $rtokens;
5032}
5033
5034#########i#############################################################
5035# Tokenizer guessing routines for ambiguous situations
5036#######################################################################
5037
5038sub guess_if_pattern_or_conditional {
5039
5040 # this routine is called when we have encountered a ? following an
5041 # unknown bareword, and we must decide if it starts a pattern or not
5042 # input parameters:
5043 # $i - token index of the ? starting possible pattern
5044 # output parameters:
5045 # $is_pattern = 0 if probably not pattern, =1 if probably a pattern
5046 # msg = a warning or diagnostic message
5047 # USES GLOBAL VARIABLES: $last_nonblank_token
5048
5049 # FIXME: this needs to be rewritten
5050
5051 my ( $i, $rtokens, $rtoken_map, $max_token_index ) = @_;
5052 my $is_pattern = 0;
5053 my $msg = "guessing that ? after $last_nonblank_token starts a ";
5054
5055 if ( $i >= $max_token_index ) {
5056 $msg .= "conditional (no end to pattern found on the line)\n";
5057 }
5058 else {
5059 my $ibeg = $i;
5060 $i = $ibeg + 1;
5061 my $next_token = $rtokens->[$i]; # first token after ?
5062
5063 # look for a possible ending ? on this line..
5064 my $in_quote = 1;
5065 my $quote_depth = 0;
5066 my $quote_character = '';
5067 my $quote_pos = 0;
5068 my $quoted_string;
5069 (
5070 $i, $in_quote, $quote_character, $quote_pos, $quote_depth,
5071 $quoted_string
5072 )
5073 = follow_quoted_string( $ibeg, $in_quote, $rtokens, $quote_character,
5074 $quote_pos, $quote_depth, $max_token_index );
5075
5076 if ($in_quote) {
5077
5078 # we didn't find an ending ? on this line,
5079 # so we bias towards conditional
5080 $is_pattern = 0;
5081 $msg .= "conditional (no ending ? on this line)\n";
5082
5083 # we found an ending ?, so we bias towards a pattern
5084 }
5085 else {
5086
5087 # Watch out for an ending ? in quotes, like this
5088 # my $case_flag = File::Spec->case_tolerant ? '(?i)' : '';
5089 my $s_quote = 0;
5090 my $d_quote = 0;
5091 my $colons = 0;
5092 foreach my $ii ( $ibeg + 1 .. $i - 1 ) {
5093 my $tok = $rtokens->[$ii];
5094 if ( $tok eq ":" ) { $colons++ }
5095 if ( $tok eq "'" ) { $s_quote++ }
5096 if ( $tok eq '"' ) { $d_quote++ }
5097 }
5098 if ( $s_quote % 2 || $d_quote % 2 || $colons ) {
5099 $is_pattern = 0;
5100 $msg .= "found ending ? but unbalanced quote chars\n";
5101 }
5102 elsif ( pattern_expected( $i, $rtokens, $max_token_index ) >= 0 ) {
5103 $is_pattern = 1;
5104 $msg .= "pattern (found ending ? and pattern expected)\n";
5105 }
5106 else {
5107 $msg .= "pattern (uncertain, but found ending ?)\n";
5108 }
5109 }
5110 }
5111 return ( $is_pattern, $msg );
5112}
5113
5114sub guess_if_pattern_or_division {
5115
5116 # this routine is called when we have encountered a / following an
5117 # unknown bareword, and we must decide if it starts a pattern or is a
5118 # division
5119 # input parameters:
5120 # $i - token index of the / starting possible pattern
5121 # output parameters:
5122 # $is_pattern = 0 if probably division, =1 if probably a pattern
5123 # msg = a warning or diagnostic message
5124 # USES GLOBAL VARIABLES: $last_nonblank_token
5125 my ( $i, $rtokens, $rtoken_map, $max_token_index ) = @_;
5126 my $is_pattern = 0;
5127 my $msg = "guessing that / after $last_nonblank_token starts a ";
5128
5129 if ( $i >= $max_token_index ) {
5130 $msg .= "division (no end to pattern found on the line)\n";
5131 }
5132 else {
5133 my $ibeg = $i;
5134 my $divide_expected =
5135 numerator_expected( $i, $rtokens, $max_token_index );
5136 $i = $ibeg + 1;
5137 my $next_token = $rtokens->[$i]; # first token after slash
5138
5139 # look for a possible ending / on this line..
5140 my $in_quote = 1;
5141 my $quote_depth = 0;
5142 my $quote_character = '';
5143 my $quote_pos = 0;
5144 my $quoted_string;
5145 (
5146 $i, $in_quote, $quote_character, $quote_pos, $quote_depth,
5147 $quoted_string
5148 )
5149 = follow_quoted_string( $ibeg, $in_quote, $rtokens, $quote_character,
5150 $quote_pos, $quote_depth, $max_token_index );
5151
5152 if ($in_quote) {
5153
5154 # we didn't find an ending / on this line,
5155 # so we bias towards division
5156 if ( $divide_expected >= 0 ) {
5157 $is_pattern = 0;
5158 $msg .= "division (no ending / on this line)\n";
5159 }
5160 else {
5161 $msg = "multi-line pattern (division not possible)\n";
5162 $is_pattern = 1;
5163 }
5164
5165 }
5166
5167 # we found an ending /, so we bias towards a pattern
5168 else {
5169
5170 if ( pattern_expected( $i, $rtokens, $max_token_index ) >= 0 ) {
5171
5172 if ( $divide_expected >= 0 ) {
5173
5174 if ( $i - $ibeg > 60 ) {
5175 $msg .= "division (matching / too distant)\n";
5176 $is_pattern = 0;
5177 }
5178 else {
5179 $msg .= "pattern (but division possible too)\n";
5180 $is_pattern = 1;
5181 }
5182 }
5183 else {
5184 $is_pattern = 1;
5185 $msg .= "pattern (division not possible)\n";
5186 }
5187 }
5188 else {
5189
5190 if ( $divide_expected >= 0 ) {
5191 $is_pattern = 0;
5192 $msg .= "division (pattern not possible)\n";
5193 }
5194 else {
5195 $is_pattern = 1;
5196 $msg .=
5197 "pattern (uncertain, but division would not work here)\n";
5198 }
5199 }
5200 }
5201 }
5202 return ( $is_pattern, $msg );
5203}
5204
5205# try to resolve here-doc vs. shift by looking ahead for
5206# non-code or the end token (currently only looks for end token)
5207# returns 1 if it is probably a here doc, 0 if not
5208sub guess_if_here_doc {
5209
5210 # This is how many lines we will search for a target as part of the
5211 # guessing strategy. It is a constant because there is probably
5212 # little reason to change it.
5213 # USES GLOBAL VARIABLES: $tokenizer_self, $current_package
5214 # %is_constant,
5215 my $HERE_DOC_WINDOW = 40;
5216
5217 my $next_token = shift;
5218 my $here_doc_expected = 0;
5219 my $line;
5220 my $k = 0;
5221 my $msg = "checking <<";
5222
5223 while ( $line = $tokenizer_self->{_line_buffer_object}->peek_ahead( $k++ ) )
5224 {
5225 chomp $line;
5226
5227 if ( $line =~ /^$next_token$/ ) {
5228 $msg .= " -- found target $next_token ahead $k lines\n";
5229 $here_doc_expected = 1; # got it
5230 last;
5231 }
5232 last if ( $k >= $HERE_DOC_WINDOW );
5233 }
5234
5235 unless ($here_doc_expected) {
5236
5237 if ( !defined($line) ) {
5238 $here_doc_expected = -1; # hit eof without seeing target
5239 $msg .= " -- must be shift; target $next_token not in file\n";
5240
5241 }
5242 else { # still unsure..taking a wild guess
5243
5244 if ( !$is_constant{$current_package}{$next_token} ) {
5245 $here_doc_expected = 1;
5246 $msg .=
5247 " -- guessing it's a here-doc ($next_token not a constant)\n";
5248 }
5249 else {
5250 $msg .=
5251 " -- guessing it's a shift ($next_token is a constant)\n";
5252 }
5253 }
5254 }
5255 write_logfile_entry($msg);
5256 return $here_doc_expected;
5257}
5258
5259#########i#############################################################
5260# Tokenizer Routines for scanning identifiers and related items
5261#######################################################################
5262
5263sub scan_bare_identifier_do {
5264
5265 # this routine is called to scan a token starting with an alphanumeric
5266 # variable or package separator, :: or '.
5267 # USES GLOBAL VARIABLES: $current_package, $last_nonblank_token,
5268 # $last_nonblank_type,@paren_type, $paren_depth
5269
5270 my ( $input_line, $i, $tok, $type, $prototype, $rtoken_map,
5271 $max_token_index )
5272 = @_;
5273 my $i_begin = $i;
5274 my $package = undef;
5275
5276 my $i_beg = $i;
5277
5278 # we have to back up one pretoken at a :: since each : is one pretoken
5279 if ( $tok eq '::' ) { $i_beg-- }
5280 if ( $tok eq '->' ) { $i_beg-- }
5281 my $pos_beg = $rtoken_map->[$i_beg];
5282 pos($input_line) = $pos_beg;
5283
5284 # Examples:
5285 # A::B::C
5286 # A::
5287 # ::A
5288 # A'B
5289 if ( $input_line =~ m/\G\s*((?:\w*(?:'|::)))*(?:(?:->)?(\w+))?/gc ) {
5290
5291 my $pos = pos($input_line);
5292 my $numc = $pos - $pos_beg;
5293 $tok = substr( $input_line, $pos_beg, $numc );
5294
5295 # type 'w' includes anything without leading type info
5296 # ($,%,@,*) including something like abc::def::ghi
5297 $type = 'w';
5298
5299 my $sub_name = "";
5300 if ( defined($2) ) { $sub_name = $2; }
5301 if ( defined($1) ) {
5302 $package = $1;
5303
5304 # patch: don't allow isolated package name which just ends
5305 # in the old style package separator (single quote). Example:
5306 # use CGI':all';
5307 if ( !($sub_name) && substr( $package, -1, 1 ) eq '\'' ) {
5308 $pos--;
5309 }
5310
5311 $package =~ s/\'/::/g;
5312 if ( $package =~ /^\:/ ) { $package = 'main' . $package }
5313 $package =~ s/::$//;
5314 }
5315 else {
5316 $package = $current_package;
5317
5318 if ( $is_keyword{$tok} ) {
5319 $type = 'k';
5320 }
5321 }
5322
5323 # if it is a bareword..
5324 if ( $type eq 'w' ) {
5325
5326 # check for v-string with leading 'v' type character
5327 # (This seems to have precedence over filehandle, type 'Y')
5328 if ( $tok =~ /^v\d[_\d]*$/ ) {
5329
5330 # we only have the first part - something like 'v101' -
5331 # look for more
5332 if ( $input_line =~ m/\G(\.\d[_\d]*)+/gc ) {
5333 $pos = pos($input_line);
5334 $numc = $pos - $pos_beg;
5335 $tok = substr( $input_line, $pos_beg, $numc );
5336 }
5337 $type = 'v';
5338
5339 # warn if this version can't handle v-strings
5340 report_v_string($tok);
5341 }
5342
5343 elsif ( $is_constant{$package}{$sub_name} ) {
5344 $type = 'C';
5345 }
5346
5347 # bareword after sort has implied empty prototype; for example:
5348 # @sorted = sort numerically ( 53, 29, 11, 32, 7 );
5349 # This has priority over whatever the user has specified.
5350 elsif ($last_nonblank_token eq 'sort'
5351 && $last_nonblank_type eq 'k' )
5352 {
5353 $type = 'Z';
5354 }
5355
5356 # Note: strangely, perl does not seem to really let you create
5357 # functions which act like eval and do, in the sense that eval
5358 # and do may have operators following the final }, but any operators
5359 # that you create with prototype (&) apparently do not allow
5360 # trailing operators, only terms. This seems strange.
5361 # If this ever changes, here is the update
5362 # to make perltidy behave accordingly:
5363
5364 # elsif ( $is_block_function{$package}{$tok} ) {
5365 # $tok='eval'; # patch to do braces like eval - doesn't work
5366 # $type = 'k';
5367 #}
5368 # FIXME: This could become a separate type to allow for different
5369 # future behavior:
5370 elsif ( $is_block_function{$package}{$sub_name} ) {
5371 $type = 'G';
5372 }
5373
5374 elsif ( $is_block_list_function{$package}{$sub_name} ) {
5375 $type = 'G';
5376 }
5377 elsif ( $is_user_function{$package}{$sub_name} ) {
5378 $type = 'U';
5379 $prototype = $user_function_prototype{$package}{$sub_name};
5380 }
5381
5382 # check for indirect object
5383 elsif (
5384
5385 # added 2001-03-27: must not be followed immediately by '('
5386 # see fhandle.t
5387 ( $input_line !~ m/\G\(/gc )
5388
5389 # and
5390 && (
5391
5392 # preceded by keyword like 'print', 'printf' and friends
5393 $is_indirect_object_taker{$last_nonblank_token}
5394
5395 # or preceded by something like 'print(' or 'printf('
5396 || (
5397 ( $last_nonblank_token eq '(' )
5398 && $is_indirect_object_taker{ $paren_type[$paren_depth]
5399 }
5400
5401 )
5402 )
5403 )
5404 {
5405
5406 # may not be indirect object unless followed by a space
5407 if ( $input_line =~ m/\G\s+/gc ) {
5408 $type = 'Y';
5409
5410 # Abandon Hope ...
5411 # Perl's indirect object notation is a very bad
5412 # thing and can cause subtle bugs, especially for
5413 # beginning programmers. And I haven't even been
5414 # able to figure out a sane warning scheme which
5415 # doesn't get in the way of good scripts.
5416
5417 # Complain if a filehandle has any lower case
5418 # letters. This is suggested good practice.
5419 # Use 'sub_name' because something like
5420 # main::MYHANDLE is ok for filehandle
5421 if ( $sub_name =~ /[a-z]/ ) {
5422
5423 # could be bug caused by older perltidy if
5424 # followed by '('
5425 if ( $input_line =~ m/\G\s*\(/gc ) {
5426 complain(
5427"Caution: unknown word '$tok' in indirect object slot\n"
5428 );
5429 }
5430 }
5431 }
5432
5433 # bareword not followed by a space -- may not be filehandle
5434 # (may be function call defined in a 'use' statement)
5435 else {
5436 $type = 'Z';
5437 }
5438 }
5439 }
5440
5441 # Now we must convert back from character position
5442 # to pre_token index.
5443 # I don't think an error flag can occur here ..but who knows
5444 my $error;
5445 ( $i, $error ) =
5446 inverse_pretoken_map( $i, $pos, $rtoken_map, $max_token_index );
5447 if ($error) {
5448 warning("scan_bare_identifier: Possibly invalid tokenization\n");
5449 }
5450 }
5451
5452 # no match but line not blank - could be syntax error
5453 # perl will take '::' alone without complaint
5454 else {
5455 $type = 'w';
5456
5457 # change this warning to log message if it becomes annoying
5458 warning("didn't find identifier after leading ::\n");
5459 }
5460 return ( $i, $tok, $type, $prototype );
5461}
5462
5463sub scan_id_do {
5464
5465# This is the new scanner and will eventually replace scan_identifier.
5466# Only type 'sub' and 'package' are implemented.
5467# Token types $ * % @ & -> are not yet implemented.
5468#
5469# Scan identifier following a type token.
5470# The type of call depends on $id_scan_state: $id_scan_state = ''
5471# for starting call, in which case $tok must be the token defining
5472# the type.
5473#
5474# If the type token is the last nonblank token on the line, a value
5475# of $id_scan_state = $tok is returned, indicating that further
5476# calls must be made to get the identifier. If the type token is
5477# not the last nonblank token on the line, the identifier is
5478# scanned and handled and a value of '' is returned.
5479# USES GLOBAL VARIABLES: $current_package, $last_nonblank_token, $in_attribute_list,
5480# $statement_type, $tokenizer_self
5481
5482 my ( $input_line, $i, $tok, $rtokens, $rtoken_map, $id_scan_state,
5483 $max_token_index )
5484 = @_;
5485 my $type = '';
5486 my ( $i_beg, $pos_beg );
5487
5488 #print "NSCAN:entering i=$i, tok=$tok, type=$type, state=$id_scan_state\n";
5489 #my ($a,$b,$c) = caller;
5490 #print "NSCAN: scan_id called with tok=$tok $a $b $c\n";
5491
5492 # on re-entry, start scanning at first token on the line
5493 if ($id_scan_state) {
5494 $i_beg = $i;
5495 $type = '';
5496 }
5497
5498 # on initial entry, start scanning just after type token
5499 else {
5500 $i_beg = $i + 1;
5501 $id_scan_state = $tok;
5502 $type = 't';
5503 }
5504
5505 # find $i_beg = index of next nonblank token,
5506 # and handle empty lines
5507 my $blank_line = 0;
5508 my $next_nonblank_token = $rtokens->[$i_beg];
5509 if ( $i_beg > $max_token_index ) {
5510 $blank_line = 1;
5511 }
5512 else {
5513
5514 # only a '#' immediately after a '$' is not a comment
5515 if ( $next_nonblank_token eq '#' ) {
5516 unless ( $tok eq '$' ) {
5517 $blank_line = 1;
5518 }
5519 }
5520
5521 if ( $next_nonblank_token =~ /^\s/ ) {
5522 ( $next_nonblank_token, $i_beg ) =
5523 find_next_nonblank_token_on_this_line( $i_beg, $rtokens,
5524 $max_token_index );
5525 if ( $next_nonblank_token =~ /(^#|^\s*$)/ ) {
5526 $blank_line = 1;
5527 }
5528 }
5529 }
5530
5531 # handle non-blank line; identifier, if any, must follow
5532 unless ($blank_line) {
5533
5534 if ( $id_scan_state eq 'sub' ) {
5535 ( $i, $tok, $type, $id_scan_state ) = do_scan_sub(
5536 $input_line, $i, $i_beg,
5537 $tok, $type, $rtokens,
5538 $rtoken_map, $id_scan_state, $max_token_index
5539 );
5540 }
5541
5542 elsif ( $id_scan_state eq 'package' ) {
5543 ( $i, $tok, $type ) =
5544 do_scan_package( $input_line, $i, $i_beg, $tok, $type, $rtokens,
5545 $rtoken_map, $max_token_index );
5546 $id_scan_state = '';
5547 }
5548
5549 else {
5550 warning("invalid token in scan_id: $tok\n");
5551 $id_scan_state = '';
5552 }
5553 }
5554
5555 if ( $id_scan_state && ( !defined($type) || !$type ) ) {
5556
5557 # shouldn't happen:
5558 warning(
5559"Program bug in scan_id: undefined type but scan_state=$id_scan_state\n"
5560 );
5561 report_definite_bug();
5562 }
5563
5564 TOKENIZER_DEBUG_FLAG_NSCAN && do {
5565 print STDOUT
5566 "NSCAN: returns i=$i, tok=$tok, type=$type, state=$id_scan_state\n";
5567 };
5568 return ( $i, $tok, $type, $id_scan_state );
5569}
5570
5571sub check_prototype {
5572 my ( $proto, $package, $subname ) = @_;
5573 return unless ( defined($package) && defined($subname) );
5574 if ( defined($proto) ) {
5575 $proto =~ s/^\s*\(\s*//;
5576 $proto =~ s/\s*\)$//;
5577 if ($proto) {
5578 $is_user_function{$package}{$subname} = 1;
5579 $user_function_prototype{$package}{$subname} = "($proto)";
5580
5581 # prototypes containing '&' must be treated specially..
5582 if ( $proto =~ /\&/ ) {
5583
5584 # right curly braces of prototypes ending in
5585 # '&' may be followed by an operator
5586 if ( $proto =~ /\&$/ ) {
5587 $is_block_function{$package}{$subname} = 1;
5588 }
5589
5590 # right curly braces of prototypes NOT ending in
5591 # '&' may NOT be followed by an operator
5592 elsif ( $proto !~ /\&$/ ) {
5593 $is_block_list_function{$package}{$subname} = 1;
5594 }
5595 }
5596 }
5597 else {
5598 $is_constant{$package}{$subname} = 1;
5599 }
5600 }
5601 else {
5602 $is_user_function{$package}{$subname} = 1;
5603 }
5604 return;
5605}
5606
5607sub do_scan_package {
5608
5609 # do_scan_package parses a package name
5610 # it is called with $i_beg equal to the index of the first nonblank
5611 # token following a 'package' token.
5612 # USES GLOBAL VARIABLES: $current_package,
5613
5614 # package NAMESPACE
5615 # package NAMESPACE VERSION
5616 # package NAMESPACE BLOCK
5617 # package NAMESPACE VERSION BLOCK
5618 #
5619 # If VERSION is provided, package sets the $VERSION variable in the given
5620 # namespace to a version object with the VERSION provided. VERSION must be
5621 # a "strict" style version number as defined by the version module: a
5622 # positive decimal number (integer or decimal-fraction) without
5623 # exponentiation or else a dotted-decimal v-string with a leading 'v'
5624 # character and at least three components.
5625 # reference http://perldoc.perl.org/functions/package.html
5626
5627 my ( $input_line, $i, $i_beg, $tok, $type, $rtokens, $rtoken_map,
5628 $max_token_index )
5629 = @_;
5630 my $package = undef;
5631 my $pos_beg = $rtoken_map->[$i_beg];
5632 pos($input_line) = $pos_beg;
5633
5634 # handle non-blank line; package name, if any, must follow
5635 if ( $input_line =~ m/\G\s*((?:\w*(?:'|::))*\w+)/gc ) {
5636 $package = $1;
5637 $package = ( defined($1) && $1 ) ? $1 : 'main';
5638 $package =~ s/\'/::/g;
5639 if ( $package =~ /^\:/ ) { $package = 'main' . $package }
5640 $package =~ s/::$//;
5641 my $pos = pos($input_line);
5642 my $numc = $pos - $pos_beg;
5643 $tok = 'package ' . substr( $input_line, $pos_beg, $numc );
5644 $type = 'i';
5645
5646 # Now we must convert back from character position
5647 # to pre_token index.
5648 # I don't think an error flag can occur here ..but ?
5649 my $error;
5650 ( $i, $error ) =
5651 inverse_pretoken_map( $i, $pos, $rtoken_map, $max_token_index );
5652 if ($error) { warning("Possibly invalid package\n") }
5653 $current_package = $package;
5654
5655 # we should now have package NAMESPACE
5656 # now expecting VERSION, BLOCK, or ; to follow ...
5657 # package NAMESPACE VERSION
5658 # package NAMESPACE BLOCK
5659 # package NAMESPACE VERSION BLOCK
5660 my ( $next_nonblank_token, $i_next ) =
5661 find_next_nonblank_token( $i, $rtokens, $max_token_index );
5662
5663 # check that something recognizable follows, but do not parse.
5664 # A VERSION number will be parsed later as a number or v-string in the
5665 # normal way. What is important is to set the statement type if
5666 # everything looks okay so that the operator_expected() routine
5667 # knows that the number is in a package statement.
5668 # Examples of valid primitive tokens that might follow are:
5669 # 1235 . ; { } v3 v
5670 if ( $next_nonblank_token =~ /^([v\.\d;\{\}])|v\d|\d+$/ ) {
5671 $statement_type = $tok;
5672 }
5673 else {
5674 warning(
5675 "Unexpected '$next_nonblank_token' after package name '$tok'\n"
5676 );
5677 }
5678 }
5679
5680 # no match but line not blank --
5681 # could be a label with name package, like package: , for example.
5682 else {
5683 $type = 'k';
5684 }
5685
5686 return ( $i, $tok, $type );
5687}
5688
5689sub scan_identifier_do {
5690
5691 # This routine assembles tokens into identifiers. It maintains a
5692 # scan state, id_scan_state. It updates id_scan_state based upon
5693 # current id_scan_state and token, and returns an updated
5694 # id_scan_state and the next index after the identifier.
5695 # USES GLOBAL VARIABLES: $context, $last_nonblank_token,
5696 # $last_nonblank_type
5697
5698 my ( $i, $id_scan_state, $identifier, $rtokens, $max_token_index,
5699 $expecting, $container_type )
5700 = @_;
5701 my $i_begin = $i;
5702 my $type = '';
5703 my $tok_begin = $rtokens->[$i_begin];
5704 if ( $tok_begin eq ':' ) { $tok_begin = '::' }
5705 my $id_scan_state_begin = $id_scan_state;
5706 my $identifier_begin = $identifier;
5707 my $tok = $tok_begin;
5708 my $message = "";
5709
5710 my $in_prototype_or_signature = $container_type =~ /^sub/;
5711
5712 # these flags will be used to help figure out the type:
5713 my $saw_alpha = ( $tok =~ /^[A-Za-z_]/ );
5714 my $saw_type;
5715
5716 # allow old package separator (') except in 'use' statement
5717 my $allow_tick = ( $last_nonblank_token ne 'use' );
5718
5719 # get started by defining a type and a state if necessary
5720 unless ($id_scan_state) {
5721 $context = UNKNOWN_CONTEXT;
5722
5723 # fixup for digraph
5724 if ( $tok eq '>' ) {
5725 $tok = '->';
5726 $tok_begin = $tok;
5727 }
5728 $identifier = $tok;
5729
5730 if ( $tok eq '$' || $tok eq '*' ) {
5731 $id_scan_state = '$';
5732 $context = SCALAR_CONTEXT;
5733 }
5734 elsif ( $tok eq '%' || $tok eq '@' ) {
5735 $id_scan_state = '$';
5736 $context = LIST_CONTEXT;
5737 }
5738 elsif ( $tok eq '&' ) {
5739 $id_scan_state = '&';
5740 }
5741 elsif ( $tok eq 'sub' or $tok eq 'package' ) {
5742 $saw_alpha = 0; # 'sub' is considered type info here
5743 $id_scan_state = '$';
5744 $identifier .= ' '; # need a space to separate sub from sub name
5745 }
5746 elsif ( $tok eq '::' ) {
5747 $id_scan_state = 'A';
5748 }
5749 elsif ( $tok =~ /^[A-Za-z_]/ ) {
5750 $id_scan_state = ':';
5751 }
5752 elsif ( $tok eq '->' ) {
5753 $id_scan_state = '$';
5754 }
5755 else {
5756
5757 # shouldn't happen
5758 my ( $a, $b, $c ) = caller;
5759 warning("Program Bug: scan_identifier given bad token = $tok \n");
5760 warning(" called from sub $a line: $c\n");
5761 report_definite_bug();
5762 }
5763 $saw_type = !$saw_alpha;
5764 }
5765 else {
5766 $i--;
5767 $saw_type = ( $tok =~ /([\$\%\@\*\&])/ );
5768 }
5769
5770 # now loop to gather the identifier
5771 my $i_save = $i;
5772
5773 while ( $i < $max_token_index ) {
5774 $i_save = $i unless ( $tok =~ /^\s*$/ );
5775 $tok = $rtokens->[ ++$i ];
5776
5777 if ( ( $tok eq ':' ) && ( $rtokens->[ $i + 1 ] eq ':' ) ) {
5778 $tok = '::';
5779 $i++;
5780 }
5781
5782 if ( $id_scan_state eq '$' ) { # starting variable name
5783
5784 if ( $tok eq '$' ) {
5785
5786 $identifier .= $tok;
5787
5788 # we've got a punctuation variable if end of line (punct.t)
5789 if ( $i == $max_token_index ) {
5790 $type = 'i';
5791 $id_scan_state = '';
5792 last;
5793 }
5794 }
5795
5796 # POSTDEFREF ->@ ->% ->& ->*
5797 elsif ( ( $tok =~ /^[\@\%\&\*]$/ ) && $identifier =~ /\-\>$/ ) {
5798 $identifier .= $tok;
5799 }
5800 elsif ( $tok =~ /^[A-Za-z_]/ ) { # alphanumeric ..
5801 $saw_alpha = 1;
5802 $id_scan_state = ':'; # now need ::
5803 $identifier .= $tok;
5804 }
5805 elsif ( $tok eq "'" && $allow_tick ) { # alphanumeric ..
5806 $saw_alpha = 1;
5807 $id_scan_state = ':'; # now need ::
5808 $identifier .= $tok;
5809
5810 # Perl will accept leading digits in identifiers,
5811 # although they may not always produce useful results.
5812 # Something like $main::0 is ok. But this also works:
5813 #
5814 # sub howdy::123::bubba{ print "bubba $54321!\n" }
5815 # howdy::123::bubba();
5816 #
5817 }
5818 elsif ( $tok =~ /^[0-9]/ ) { # numeric
5819 $saw_alpha = 1;
5820 $id_scan_state = ':'; # now need ::
5821 $identifier .= $tok;
5822 }
5823 elsif ( $tok eq '::' ) {
5824 $id_scan_state = 'A';
5825 $identifier .= $tok;
5826 }
5827
5828 # $# and POSTDEFREF ->$#
5829 elsif ( ( $tok eq '#' ) && ( $identifier =~ /\$$/ ) ) { # $#array
5830 $identifier .= $tok; # keep same state, a $ could follow
5831 }
5832 elsif ( $tok eq '{' ) {
5833
5834 # check for something like ${#} or ${�}
5835 if (
5836 (
5837 $identifier eq '$'
5838 || $identifier eq '@'
5839 || $identifier eq '$#'
5840 )
5841 && $i + 2 <= $max_token_index
5842 && $rtokens->[ $i + 2 ] eq '}'
5843 && $rtokens->[ $i + 1 ] !~ /[\s\w]/
5844 )
5845 {
5846 my $next2 = $rtokens->[ $i + 2 ];
5847 my $next1 = $rtokens->[ $i + 1 ];
5848 $identifier .= $tok . $next1 . $next2;
5849 $i += 2;
5850 $id_scan_state = '';
5851 last;
5852 }
5853
5854 # skip something like ${xxx} or ->{
5855 $id_scan_state = '';
5856
5857 # if this is the first token of a line, any tokens for this
5858 # identifier have already been accumulated
5859 if ( $identifier eq '$' || $i == 0 ) { $identifier = ''; }
5860 $i = $i_save;
5861 last;
5862 }
5863
5864 # space ok after leading $ % * & @
5865 elsif ( $tok =~ /^\s*$/ ) {
5866
5867 if ( $identifier =~ /^[\$\%\*\&\@]/ ) {
5868
5869 if ( length($identifier) > 1 ) {
5870 $id_scan_state = '';
5871 $i = $i_save;
5872 $type = 'i'; # probably punctuation variable
5873 last;
5874 }
5875 else {
5876
5877 # spaces after $'s are common, and space after @
5878 # is harmless, so only complain about space
5879 # after other type characters. Space after $ and
5880 # @ will be removed in formatting. Report space
5881 # after % and * because they might indicate a
5882 # parsing error. In other words '% ' might be a
5883 # modulo operator. Delete this warning if it
5884 # gets annoying.
5885 if ( $identifier !~ /^[\@\$]$/ ) {
5886 $message =
5887 "Space in identifier, following $identifier\n";
5888 }
5889 }
5890 }
5891
5892 # else:
5893 # space after '->' is ok
5894 }
5895 elsif ( $tok eq '^' ) {
5896
5897 # check for some special variables like $^W
5898 if ( $identifier =~ /^[\$\*\@\%]$/ ) {
5899 $identifier .= $tok;
5900 $id_scan_state = 'A';
5901
5902 # Perl accepts '$^]' or '@^]', but
5903 # there must not be a space before the ']'.
5904 my $next1 = $rtokens->[ $i + 1 ];
5905 if ( $next1 eq ']' ) {
5906 $i++;
5907 $identifier .= $next1;
5908 $id_scan_state = "";
5909 last;
5910 }
5911 }
5912 else {
5913 $id_scan_state = '';
5914 }
5915 }
5916 else { # something else
5917
5918 if ( $in_prototype_or_signature && $tok =~ /^[\),=]/ ) {
5919 $id_scan_state = '';
5920 $i = $i_save;
5921 $type = 'i'; # probably punctuation variable
5922 last;
5923 }
5924
5925 # check for various punctuation variables
5926 if ( $identifier =~ /^[\$\*\@\%]$/ ) {
5927 $identifier .= $tok;
5928 }
5929
5930 # POSTDEFREF: Postfix reference ->$* ->%* ->@* ->** ->&* ->$#*

5936

5941 $type = 'i';
5942 $identifier .= $tok;
5943 }

5945 $i = $i_save;
5946 write_logfile_entry( 'Use of $# is deprecated' . "\n" );
5947 }
5948 }

5950
5951 # perl does not allow references to punctuation
5952 # variables without braces. For example, this
5953 # won't work:
5954 # $:=\4;
5955 # $a = $$:;
5956 # You would have to use
5957 # $a = ${$:};

5961 else { $type = 'i' }
5962 }

5965 }

5967 $i = $i_save;

5972 }
5973 }

5975

5977 $id_scan_state = ':'; # now need ::

5992 }

5996 }
5997 elsif ( $tok eq '{' ) {
5998 if ( $identifier eq '&' || $i == 0 ) { $identifier = ''; }
5999 $i = $i_save;
6000 $id_scan_state = '';
6001 last;
6002 }

6004
6005 # punctuation variable?
6006 # testfile: cunningham4.pl
6007 #
6008 # We have to be careful here. If we are in an unknown state,
6009 # we will reject the punctuation variable. In the following
6010 # example the '&' is a binary operator but we are in an unknown
6011 # state because there is no sigil on 'Prima', so we don't
6012 # know what it is. But it is a bad guess that
6013 # '&~' is a function variable.
6014 # $self->{text}->{colorMap}->[
6015 # Prima::PodView::COLOR_CODE_FOREGROUND
6016 # & ~tb::COLOR_INDEX ] =
6017 # $sec->{ColorCode}

6019 $identifier .= $tok;
6020 }
6021 else {
6022 $identifier = '';
6023 $i = $i_save;
6024 $type = '&';
6025 }
6026 $id_scan_state = '';
6027 last;
6028 }
6029 }

6031
6032 if ( $tok =~ /^[A-Za-z_]/ ) { # found it
6033 $identifier .= $tok;
6034 $id_scan_state = ':'; # now need ::
6035 $saw_alpha = 1;
6036 }

6038 $identifier .= $tok;
6039 $id_scan_state = ':'; # now need ::
6040 $saw_alpha = 1;
6041 }
6042 elsif ( $tok =~ /^[0-9]/ ) { # numeric..see comments above
6043 $identifier .= $tok;
6044 $id_scan_state = ':'; # now need ::
6045 $saw_alpha = 1;
6046 }

6048 $id_scan_state = '(';
6049 $identifier .= $tok;
6050 }
6051 elsif ( ( $identifier =~ /^sub / ) && ( $tok eq '(' ) ) {
6052 $id_scan_state = ')';
6053 $identifier .= $tok;
6054 }
6055 else {
6056 $id_scan_state = '';
6057 $i = $i_save;
6058 last;
6059 }
6060 }
6061 elsif ( $id_scan_state eq ':' ) { # looking for :: after alpha
6062
6063 if ( $tok eq '::' ) { # got it
6064 $identifier .= $tok;
6065 $id_scan_state = 'A'; # now require alpha
6066 }
6067 elsif ( $tok =~ /^[A-Za-z_]/ ) { # more alphanumeric is ok here
6068 $identifier .= $tok;
6069 $id_scan_state = ':'; # now need ::
6070 $saw_alpha = 1;
6071 }
6072 elsif ( $tok =~ /^[0-9]/ ) { # numeric..see comments above
6073 $identifier .= $tok;
6074 $id_scan_state = ':'; # now need ::
6075 $saw_alpha = 1;
6076 }

6078
6079 if ( $is_keyword{$identifier} ) {
6080 $id_scan_state = ''; # that's all
6081 $i = $i_save;
6082 }
6083 else {
6084 $identifier .= $tok;
6085 }
6086 }
6087 elsif ( ( $identifier =~ /^sub / ) && ( $tok =~ /^\s*$/ ) ) {
6088 $id_scan_state = '(';
6089 $identifier .= $tok;
6090 }
6091 elsif ( ( $identifier =~ /^sub / ) && ( $tok eq '(' ) ) {
6092 $id_scan_state = ')';
6093 $identifier .= $tok;
6094 }
6095 else {
6096 $id_scan_state = ''; # that's all
6097 $i = $i_save;
6098 last;
6099 }
6100 }
6101 elsif ( $id_scan_state eq '(' ) { # looking for ( of prototype
6102
6103 if ( $tok eq '(' ) { # got it
6104 $identifier .= $tok;
6105 $id_scan_state = ')'; # now find the end of it
6106 }
6107 elsif ( $tok =~ /^\s*$/ ) { # blank - keep going
6108 $identifier .= $tok;
6109 }
6110 else {
6111 $id_scan_state = ''; # that's all - no prototype
6112 $i = $i_save;
6113 last;
6114 }
6115 }
6116 elsif ( $id_scan_state eq ')' ) { # looking for ) to end
6117
6118 if ( $tok eq ')' ) { # got it
6119 $identifier .= $tok;
6120 $id_scan_state = ''; # all done
6121 last;
6122 }
6123 elsif ( $tok =~ /^[\s\$\%\\\*\@\&\;]/ ) {
6124 $identifier .= $tok;
6125 }
6126 else { # probable error in script, but keep going
6127 warning("Unexpected '$tok' while seeking end of prototype\n");
6128 $identifier .= $tok;
6129 }
6130 }
6131 else { # can get here due to error in initialization
6132 $id_scan_state = '';
6133 $i = $i_save;
6134 last;
6135 }
6136 }
6137
6138 if ( $id_scan_state eq ')' ) {
6139 warning("Hit end of line while seeking ) to end prototype\n");
6140 }

6142 # once we enter the actual identifier, it may not extend beyond
6143 # the end of the current line
6144 if ( $id_scan_state =~ /^[A\:\(\)]/ ) {
6145 $id_scan_state = '';
6146 }
6147 if ( $i < 0 ) { $i = 0 }
6148
6149 unless ($type) {
6150
6151 if ($saw_type) {
6152
6153 if ($saw_alpha) {
6154 if ( $identifier =~ /^->/ && $last_nonblank_type eq 'w' ) {
6155 $type = 'w';
6156 }
6157 else { $type = 'i' }
6158 }
6159 elsif ( $identifier eq '->' ) {
6160 $type = '->';
6161 }
6162 elsif (
6163 ( length($identifier) > 1 )
6164
6165 # In something like '@$=' we have an identifier '@$'
6166 # In something like '$${' we have type '$$' (and only
6167 # part of an identifier)
6168 && !( $identifier =~ /\$$/ && $tok eq '{' )
6169 && ( $identifier !~ /^(sub |package )$/ )
6170 )
6171 {
6172 $type = 'i';
6173 }
6174 else { $type = 't' }
6175 }

6177
6178 # type 'w' includes anything without leading type info
6179 # ($,%,@,*) including something like abc::def::ghi
6180 $type = 'w';
6181 }
6182 else {
6183 $type = '';
6184 } # this can happen on a restart
6185 }
6186
6187 if ($identifier) {
6188 $tok = $identifier;
6189 if ($message) { write_logfile_entry($message) }
6190 }
6191 else {
6192 $tok = $tok_begin;
6193 $i = $i_begin;
6194 }
6195
6196 TOKENIZER_DEBUG_FLAG_SCAN_ID && do {
6197 my ( $a, $b, $c ) = caller;
6198 print STDOUT
6199"SCANID: called from $a $b $c with tok, i, state, identifier =$tok_begin, $i_begin, $id_scan_state_begin, $identifier_begin\n";
6200 print STDOUT
6201"SCANID: returned with tok, i, state, identifier =$tok, $i, $id_scan_state, $identifier\n";
6202 };
6203 return ( $i, $tok, $type, $id_scan_state, $identifier );
6204}

6211 sub do_scan_sub {
6212
6213 # do_scan_sub parses a sub name and prototype
6214 # it is called with $i_beg equal to the index of the first nonblank
6215 # token following a 'sub' token.
6216
6217 # TODO: add future error checks to be sure we have a valid
6218 # sub name. For example, 'sub &doit' is wrong. Also, be sure
6219 # a name is given if and only if a non-anonymous sub is
6220 # appropriate.
6221 # USES GLOBAL VARS: $current_package, $last_nonblank_token,
6222 # $in_attribute_list, %saw_function_definition,
6223 # $statement_type
6224
6225 my (
6226 $input_line, $i, $i_beg,
6227 $tok, $type, $rtokens,
6228 $rtoken_map, $id_scan_state, $max_token_index
6229 ) = @_;
6230 $id_scan_state = ""; # normally we get everything in one call
6231 my $subname = undef;
6232 my $package = undef;
6233 my $proto = undef;
6234 my $attrs = undef;
6235 my $match;
6236
6237 my $pos_beg = $rtoken_map->[$i_beg];
6238 pos($input_line) = $pos_beg;
6239
6240 # Look for the sub NAME
6241 if (
6242 $input_line =~ m/\G\s*
6243 ((?:\w*(?:'|::))*) # package - something that ends in :: or '
6244 (\w+) # NAME - required
6245 /gcx
6246 )
6247 {
6248 $match = 1;
6249 $subname = $2;
6250
6251 $package = ( defined($1) && $1 ) ? $1 : $current_package;
6252 $package =~ s/\'/::/g;
6253 if ( $package =~ /^\:/ ) { $package = 'main' . $package }
6254 $package =~ s/::$//;
6255 my $pos = pos($input_line);
6256 my $numc = $pos - $pos_beg;
6257 $tok = 'sub ' . substr( $input_line, $pos_beg, $numc );
6258 $type = 'i';
6259 }
6260
6261 # Now look for PROTO ATTRS
6262 # Look for prototype/attributes which are usually on the same
6263 # line as the sub name but which might be on a separate line.
6264 # For example, we might have an anonymous sub with attributes,
6265 # or a prototype on a separate line from its sub name
6266
6267 # NOTE: We only want to parse PROTOTYPES here. If we see anything that
6268 # does not look like a prototype, we assume it is a SIGNATURE and we
6269 # will stop and let the the standard tokenizer handle it. In
6270 # particular, we stop if we see any nested parens, braces, or commas.
6271 my $saw_opening_paren = $input_line =~ /\G\s*\(/;
6272 if (
6273 $input_line =~ m/\G(\s*\([^\)\(\}\{\,]*\))? # PROTO
6274 (\s*:)? # ATTRS leading ':'
6275 /gcx
6276 && ( $1 || $2 )
6277 )
6278 {
6279 $proto = $1;
6280 $attrs = $2;
6281
6282 # If we also found the sub name on this call then append PROTO.
6283 # This is not necessary but for compatibility with previous
6284 # versions when the -csc flag is used:
6285 if ( $match && $proto ) {
6286 $tok .= $proto;
6287 }
6288 $match ||= 1;
6289
6290 # Handle prototype on separate line from subname
6291 if ($subname_saved) {
6292 $package = $package_saved;
6293 $subname = $subname_saved;
6294 $tok = $last_nonblank_token;
6295 }
6296 $type = 'i';
6297 }
6298
6299 if ($match) {
6300
6301 # ATTRS: if there are attributes, back up and let the ':' be
6302 # found later by the scanner.
6303 my $pos = pos($input_line);
6304 if ($attrs) {
6305 $pos -= length($attrs);
6306 }
6307
6308 my $next_nonblank_token = $tok;
6309
6310 # catch case of line with leading ATTR ':' after anonymous sub
6311 if ( $pos == $pos_beg && $tok eq ':' ) {
6312 $type = 'A';
6313 $in_attribute_list = 1;
6314 }
6315
6316 # Otherwise, if we found a match we must convert back from
6317 # string position to the pre_token index for continued parsing.
6318 else {
6319
6320 # I don't think an error flag can occur here ..but ?
6321 my $error;
6322 ( $i, $error ) = inverse_pretoken_map( $i, $pos, $rtoken_map,
6323 $max_token_index );
6324 if ($error) { warning("Possibly invalid sub\n") }
6325
6326 # check for multiple definitions of a sub
6327 ( $next_nonblank_token, my $i_next ) =
6328 find_next_nonblank_token_on_this_line( $i, $rtokens,
6329 $max_token_index );
6330 }
6331
6332 if ( $next_nonblank_token =~ /^(\s*|#)$/ )
6333 { # skip blank or side comment
6334 my ( $rpre_tokens, $rpre_types ) =
6335 peek_ahead_for_n_nonblank_pre_tokens(1);
6336 if ( defined($rpre_tokens) && @{$rpre_tokens} ) {
6337 $next_nonblank_token = $rpre_tokens->[0];
6338 }
6339 else {
6340 $next_nonblank_token = '}';
6341 }
6342 }
6343 $package_saved = "";
6344 $subname_saved = "";
6345
6346 # See what's next...
6347 if ( $next_nonblank_token eq '{' ) {
6348 if ($subname) {
6349
6350 # Check for multiple definitions of a sub, but
6351 # it is ok to have multiple sub BEGIN, etc,
6352 # so we do not complain if name is all caps
6353 if ( $saw_function_definition{$package}{$subname}
6354 && $subname !~ /^[A-Z]+$/ )
6355 {
6356 my $lno = $saw_function_definition{$package}{$subname};
6357 warning(
6358"already saw definition of 'sub $subname' in package '$package' at line $lno\n"
6359 );
6360 }
6361 $saw_function_definition{$package}{$subname} =
6362 $tokenizer_self->{_last_line_number};
6363 }
6364 }
6365 elsif ( $next_nonblank_token eq ';' ) {
6366 }
6367 elsif ( $next_nonblank_token eq '}' ) {
6368 }
6369
6370 # ATTRS - if an attribute list follows, remember the name
6371 # of the sub so the next opening brace can be labeled.
6372 # Setting 'statement_type' causes any ':'s to introduce
6373 # attributes.
6374 elsif ( $next_nonblank_token eq ':' ) {
6375 $statement_type = $tok;
6376 }
6377
6378 # if we stopped before an open paren ...
6379 elsif ( $next_nonblank_token eq '(' ) {
6380
6381 # If we DID NOT see this paren above then it must be on the
6382 # next line so we will set a flag to come back here and see if
6383 # it is a PROTOTYPE
6384
6385 # Otherwise, we assume it is a SIGNATURE rather than a
6386 # PROTOTYPE and let the normal tokenizer handle it as a list
6387 if ( !$saw_opening_paren ) {
6388 $id_scan_state = 'sub'; # we must come back to get proto
6389 $package_saved = $package;
6390 $subname_saved = $subname;
6391 }
6392 $statement_type = $tok;
6393 }
6394 elsif ($next_nonblank_token) { # EOF technically ok
6395 warning(
6396"expecting ':' or ';' or '{' after definition or declaration of sub '$subname' but saw '$next_nonblank_token'\n"
6397 );
6398 }
6399 check_prototype( $proto, $package, $subname );
6400 }
6401
6402 # no match but line not blank
6403 else {
6404 }
6405 return ( $i, $tok, $type, $id_scan_state );
6406 }
6407}

6409#########i###############################################################
6410# Tokenizer utility routines which may use CONSTANTS but no other GLOBALS
6411#########################################################################
6412
64131100nssub find_next_nonblank_token {
6414 my ( $i, $rtokens, $max_token_index ) = @_;
6415
6416 if ( $i >= $max_token_index ) {
6417 if ( !peeked_ahead() ) {
6418 peeked_ahead(1);
6419 $rtokens =
6420 peek_ahead_for_nonblank_token( $rtokens, $max_token_index );
6421 }
6422 }
6423 my $next_nonblank_token = $rtokens->[ ++$i ];
6424
6425 if ( $next_nonblank_token =~ /^\s*$/ ) {
6426 $next_nonblank_token = $rtokens->[ ++$i ];
6427 }
6428 return ( $next_nonblank_token, $i );
6429}

6431sub numerator_expected {
6432
6433 # this is a filter for a possible numerator, in support of guessing
6434 # for the / pattern delimiter token.
6435 # returns -
6436 # 1 - yes
6437 # 0 - can't tell
6438 # -1 - no
6439 # Note: I am using the convention that variables ending in
6440 # _expected have these 3 possible values.
6441 my ( $i, $rtokens, $max_token_index ) = @_;
6442 my $numerator_expected = 0;
6443
6444 my $next_token = $rtokens->[ $i + 1 ];
6445 if ( $next_token eq '=' ) { $i++; } # handle /=
6446 my ( $next_nonblank_token, $i_next ) =
6447 find_next_nonblank_token( $i, $rtokens, $max_token_index );
6448
6449 if ( $next_nonblank_token =~ /(\(|\$|\w|\.|\@)/ ) {
6450 $numerator_expected = 1;
6451 }
6452 else {
6453
6454 if ( $next_nonblank_token =~ /^\s*$/ ) {
6455 $numerator_expected = 0;
6456 }
6457 else {
6458 $numerator_expected = -1;
6459 }
6460 }
6461 return $numerator_expected;
6462}
6463
6464sub pattern_expected {
6465
6466 # This is the start of a filter for a possible pattern.
6467 # It looks at the token after a possible pattern and tries to
6468 # determine if that token could end a pattern.
6469 # returns -
6470 # 1 - yes
6471 # 0 - can't tell
6472 # -1 - no
6473 my ( $i, $rtokens, $max_token_index ) = @_;
6474 my $is_pattern = 0;
6475
6476 my $next_token = $rtokens->[ $i + 1 ];
6477 if ( $next_token =~ /^[msixpodualgc]/ ) { $i++; } # skip possible modifier
6478 my ( $next_nonblank_token, $i_next ) =
6479 find_next_nonblank_token( $i, $rtokens, $max_token_index );
6480
6481 # list of tokens which may follow a pattern
6482 # (can probably be expanded)
6483 if ( $next_nonblank_token =~ /(\)|\}|\;|\&\&|\|\||and|or|while|if|unless)/ )
6484 {
6485 $is_pattern = 1;
6486 }
6487 else {
6488
6489 if ( $next_nonblank_token =~ /^\s*$/ ) {
6490 $is_pattern = 0;
6491 }
6492 else {
6493 $is_pattern = -1;
6494 }
6495 }
6496 return $is_pattern;
6497}
6498
6499sub find_next_nonblank_token_on_this_line {
6500 my ( $i, $rtokens, $max_token_index ) = @_;
6501 my $next_nonblank_token;
6502
6503 if ( $i < $max_token_index ) {
6504 $next_nonblank_token = $rtokens->[ ++$i ];
6505
6506 if ( $next_nonblank_token =~ /^\s*$/ ) {
6507
6508 if ( $i < $max_token_index ) {
6509 $next_nonblank_token = $rtokens->[ ++$i ];
6510 }
6511 }
6512 }
6513 else {
6514 $next_nonblank_token = "";
6515 }
6516 return ( $next_nonblank_token, $i );
6517}

6519sub find_angle_operator_termination {
6520
6521 # We are looking at a '<' and want to know if it is an angle operator.
6522 # We are to return:
6523 # $i = pretoken index of ending '>' if found, current $i otherwise
6524 # $type = 'Q' if found, '>' otherwise
6525 my ( $input_line, $i_beg, $rtoken_map, $expecting, $max_token_index ) = @_;
6526 my $i = $i_beg;
6527 my $type = '<';
6528 pos($input_line) = 1 + $rtoken_map->[$i];
6529
6530 my $filter;
6531
6532 # we just have to find the next '>' if a term is expected
6533 if ( $expecting == TERM ) { $filter = '[\>]' }
6534
6535 # we have to guess if we don't know what is expected
6536 elsif ( $expecting == UNKNOWN ) { $filter = '[\>\;\=\#\|\<]' }
6537
6538 # shouldn't happen - we shouldn't be here if operator is expected
6539 else { warning("Program Bug in find_angle_operator_termination\n") }
6540
6541 # To illustrate what we might be looking at, in case we are
6542 # guessing, here are some examples of valid angle operators
6543 # (or file globs):
6544 # <tmp_imp/*>
6545 # <FH>
6546 # <$fh>
6547 # <*.c *.h>
6548 # <_>
6549 # <jskdfjskdfj* op/* jskdjfjkosvk*> ( glob.t)
6550 # <${PREFIX}*img*.$IMAGE_TYPE>
6551 # <img*.$IMAGE_TYPE>
6552 # <Timg*.$IMAGE_TYPE>
6553 # <$LATEX2HTMLVERSIONS${dd}html[1-9].[0-9].pl>
6554 #
6555 # Here are some examples of lines which do not have angle operators:
6556 # return unless $self->[2]++ < $#{$self->[1]};
6557 # < 2 || @$t >
6558 #
6559 # the following line from dlister.pl caused trouble:
6560 # print'~'x79,"\n",$D<1024?"0.$D":$D>>10,"K, $C files\n\n\n";
6561 #
6562 # If the '<' starts an angle operator, it must end on this line and
6563 # it must not have certain characters like ';' and '=' in it. I use
6564 # this to limit the testing. This filter should be improved if
6565 # possible.
6566
6567 if ( $input_line =~ /($filter)/g ) {
6568
6569 if ( $1 eq '>' ) {
6570
6571 # We MAY have found an angle operator termination if we get
6572 # here, but we need to do more to be sure we haven't been
6573 # fooled.
6574 my $pos = pos($input_line);
6575
6576 my $pos_beg = $rtoken_map->[$i];
6577 my $str = substr( $input_line, $pos_beg, ( $pos - $pos_beg ) );
6578
6579 # Reject if the closing '>' follows a '-' as in:
6580 # if ( VERSION < 5.009 && $op-> name eq 'assign' ) { }
6581 if ( $expecting eq UNKNOWN ) {
6582 my $check = substr( $input_line, $pos - 2, 1 );
6583 if ( $check eq '-' ) {
6584 return ( $i, $type );
6585 }
6586 }
6587
6588 ######################################debug#####
6589 #write_diagnostics( "ANGLE? :$str\n");
6590 #print "ANGLE: found $1 at pos=$pos str=$str check=$check\n";
6591 ######################################debug#####
6592 $type = 'Q';
6593 my $error;
6594 ( $i, $error ) =
6595 inverse_pretoken_map( $i, $pos, $rtoken_map, $max_token_index );
6596
6597 # It may be possible that a quote ends midway in a pretoken.
6598 # If this happens, it may be necessary to split the pretoken.
6599 if ($error) {
6600 warning(
6601 "Possible tokinization error..please check this line\n");
6602 report_possible_bug();
6603 }
6604
6605 # Now let's see where we stand....
6606 # OK if math op not possible
6607 if ( $expecting == TERM ) {
6608 }
6609
6610 # OK if there are no more than 2 pre-tokens inside
6611 # (not possible to write 2 token math between < and >)
6612 # This catches most common cases
6613 elsif ( $i <= $i_beg + 3 ) {
6614 write_diagnostics("ANGLE(1 or 2 tokens): $str\n");
6615 }
6616
6617 # Not sure..
6618 else {
6619
6620 # Let's try a Brace Test: any braces inside must balance
6621 my $br = 0;
6622 while ( $str =~ /\{/g ) { $br++ }
6623 while ( $str =~ /\}/g ) { $br-- }
6624 my $sb = 0;
6625 while ( $str =~ /\[/g ) { $sb++ }
6626 while ( $str =~ /\]/g ) { $sb-- }
6627 my $pr = 0;
6628 while ( $str =~ /\(/g ) { $pr++ }
6629 while ( $str =~ /\)/g ) { $pr-- }
6630
6631 # if braces do not balance - not angle operator
6632 if ( $br || $sb || $pr ) {
6633 $i = $i_beg;
6634 $type = '<';
6635 write_diagnostics(
6636 "NOT ANGLE (BRACE={$br ($pr [$sb ):$str\n");
6637 }
6638
6639 # we should keep doing more checks here...to be continued
6640 # Tentatively accepting this as a valid angle operator.
6641 # There are lots more things that can be checked.
6642 else {
6643 write_diagnostics(
6644 "ANGLE-Guessing yes: $str expecting=$expecting\n");
6645 write_logfile_entry("Guessing angle operator here: $str\n");
6646 }
6647 }
6648 }
6649
6650 # didn't find ending >
6651 else {
6652 if ( $expecting == TERM ) {
6653 warning("No ending > for angle operator\n");
6654 }
6655 }
6656 }
6657 return ( $i, $type );
6658}
6659
6660sub scan_number_do {
6661
6662 # scan a number in any of the formats that Perl accepts
6663 # Underbars (_) are allowed in decimal numbers.
6664 # input parameters -
6665 # $input_line - the string to scan
6666 # $i - pre_token index to start scanning
6667 # $rtoken_map - reference to the pre_token map giving starting
6668 # character position in $input_line of token $i
6669 # output parameters -
6670 # $i - last pre_token index of the number just scanned
6671 # number - the number (characters); or undef if not a number
6672
6673 my ( $input_line, $i, $rtoken_map, $input_type, $max_token_index ) = @_;
6674 my $pos_beg = $rtoken_map->[$i];
6675 my $pos;
6676 my $i_begin = $i;
6677 my $number = undef;
6678 my $type = $input_type;
6679
6680 my $first_char = substr( $input_line, $pos_beg, 1 );
6681
6682 # Look for bad starting characters; Shouldn't happen..
6683 if ( $first_char !~ /[\d\.\+\-Ee]/ ) {
6684 warning("Program bug - scan_number given character $first_char\n");
6685 report_definite_bug();
6686 return ( $i, $type, $number );
6687 }
6688
6689 # handle v-string without leading 'v' character ('Two Dot' rule)
6690 # (vstring.t)
6691 # TODO: v-strings may contain underscores
6692 pos($input_line) = $pos_beg;
6693 if ( $input_line =~ /\G((\d+)?\.\d+(\.\d+)+)/g ) {
6694 $pos = pos($input_line);
6695 my $numc = $pos - $pos_beg;
6696 $number = substr( $input_line, $pos_beg, $numc );
6697 $type = 'v';
6698 report_v_string($number);
6699 }
6700
6701 # handle octal, hex, binary
6702 if ( !defined($number) ) {
6703 pos($input_line) = $pos_beg;
6704 if ( $input_line =~
6705 /\G[+-]?0(([xX][0-9a-fA-F_]+)|([0-7_]+)|([bB][01_]+))/g )
6706 {
6707 $pos = pos($input_line);
6708 my $numc = $pos - $pos_beg;
6709 $number = substr( $input_line, $pos_beg, $numc );
6710 $type = 'n';
6711 }
6712 }
6713
6714 # handle decimal
6715 if ( !defined($number) ) {
6716 pos($input_line) = $pos_beg;
6717
6718 if ( $input_line =~ /\G([+-]?[\d_]*(\.[\d_]*)?([Ee][+-]?(\d+))?)/g ) {
6719 $pos = pos($input_line);
6720
6721 # watch out for things like 0..40 which would give 0. by this;
6722 if ( ( substr( $input_line, $pos - 1, 1 ) eq '.' )
6723 && ( substr( $input_line, $pos, 1 ) eq '.' ) )
6724 {
6725 $pos--;
6726 }
6727 my $numc = $pos - $pos_beg;
6728 $number = substr( $input_line, $pos_beg, $numc );
6729 $type = 'n';
6730 }
6731 }
6732
6733 # filter out non-numbers like e + - . e2 .e3 +e6
6734 # the rule: at least one digit, and any 'e' must be preceded by a digit
6735 if (
6736 $number !~ /\d/ # no digits
6737 || ( $number =~ /^(.*)[eE]/
6738 && $1 !~ /\d/ ) # or no digits before the 'e'
6739 )
6740 {
6741 $number = undef;
6742 $type = $input_type;
6743 return ( $i, $type, $number );
6744 }
6745
6746 # Found a number; now we must convert back from character position
6747 # to pre_token index. An error here implies user syntax error.
6748 # An example would be an invalid octal number like '009'.
6749 my $error;
6750 ( $i, $error ) =
6751 inverse_pretoken_map( $i, $pos, $rtoken_map, $max_token_index );
6752 if ($error) { warning("Possibly invalid number\n") }
6753
6754 return ( $i, $type, $number );
6755}
6756
6757sub inverse_pretoken_map {
6758
6759 # Starting with the current pre_token index $i, scan forward until
6760 # finding the index of the next pre_token whose position is $pos.
6761 my ( $i, $pos, $rtoken_map, $max_token_index ) = @_;
6762 my $error = 0;
6763
6764 while ( ++$i <= $max_token_index ) {
6765
6766 if ( $pos <= $rtoken_map->[$i] ) {
6767
6768 # Let the calling routine handle errors in which we do not
6769 # land on a pre-token boundary. It can happen by running
6770 # perltidy on some non-perl scripts, for example.
6771 if ( $pos < $rtoken_map->[$i] ) { $error = 1 }
6772 $i--;
6773 last;
6774 }
6775 }
6776 return ( $i, $error );
6777}
6778
6779sub find_here_doc {
6780
6781 # find the target of a here document, if any
6782 # input parameters:
6783 # $i - token index of the second < of <<
6784 # ($i must be less than the last token index if this is called)
6785 # output parameters:
6786 # $found_target = 0 didn't find target; =1 found target
6787 # HERE_TARGET - the target string (may be empty string)
6788 # $i - unchanged if not here doc,
6789 # or index of the last token of the here target
6790 # $saw_error - flag noting unbalanced quote on here target
6791 my ( $expecting, $i, $rtokens, $rtoken_map, $max_token_index ) = @_;
6792 my $ibeg = $i;
6793 my $found_target = 0;
6794 my $here_doc_target = '';
6795 my $here_quote_character = '';
6796 my $saw_error = 0;
6797 my ( $next_nonblank_token, $i_next_nonblank, $next_token );
6798 $next_token = $rtokens->[ $i + 1 ];
6799
6800 # perl allows a backslash before the target string (heredoc.t)
6801 my $backslash = 0;
6802 if ( $next_token eq '\\' ) {
6803 $backslash = 1;
6804 $next_token = $rtokens->[ $i + 2 ];
6805 }
6806
6807 ( $next_nonblank_token, $i_next_nonblank ) =
6808 find_next_nonblank_token_on_this_line( $i, $rtokens, $max_token_index );
6809
6810 if ( $next_nonblank_token =~ /[\'\"\`]/ ) {
6811
6812 my $in_quote = 1;
6813 my $quote_depth = 0;
6814 my $quote_pos = 0;
6815 my $quoted_string;
6816
6817 (
6818 $i, $in_quote, $here_quote_character, $quote_pos, $quote_depth,
6819 $quoted_string
6820 )
6821 = follow_quoted_string( $i_next_nonblank, $in_quote, $rtokens,
6822 $here_quote_character, $quote_pos, $quote_depth, $max_token_index );
6823
6824 if ($in_quote) { # didn't find end of quote, so no target found
6825 $i = $ibeg;
6826 if ( $expecting == TERM ) {
6827 warning(
6828"Did not find here-doc string terminator ($here_quote_character) before end of line \n"
6829 );
6830 $saw_error = 1;
6831 }
6832 }
6833 else { # found ending quote
6834 $found_target = 1;
6835
6836 my $tokj;
6837 foreach my $j ( $i_next_nonblank + 1 .. $i - 1 ) {
6838 $tokj = $rtokens->[$j];
6839
6840 # we have to remove any backslash before the quote character
6841 # so that the here-doc-target exactly matches this string
6842 next
6843 if ( $tokj eq "\\"
6844 && $j < $i - 1
6845 && $rtokens->[ $j + 1 ] eq $here_quote_character );
6846 $here_doc_target .= $tokj;
6847 }
6848 }
6849 }
6850
6851 elsif ( ( $next_token =~ /^\s*$/ ) and ( $expecting == TERM ) ) {
6852 $found_target = 1;
6853 write_logfile_entry(
6854 "found blank here-target after <<; suggest using \"\"\n");
6855 $i = $ibeg;
6856 }
6857 elsif ( $next_token =~ /^\w/ ) { # simple bareword or integer after <<
6858
6859 my $here_doc_expected;
6860 if ( $expecting == UNKNOWN ) {
6861 $here_doc_expected = guess_if_here_doc($next_token);
6862 }
6863 else {
6864 $here_doc_expected = 1;
6865 }
6866
6867 if ($here_doc_expected) {
6868 $found_target = 1;
6869 $here_doc_target = $next_token;
6870 $i = $ibeg + 1;
6871 }
6872
6873 }
6874 else {
6875
6876 if ( $expecting == TERM ) {
6877 $found_target = 1;
6878 write_logfile_entry("Note: bare here-doc operator <<\n");
6879 }
6880 else {
6881 $i = $ibeg;
6882 }
6883 }
6884
6885 # patch to neglect any prepended backslash
6886 if ( $found_target && $backslash ) { $i++ }
6887
6888 return ( $found_target, $here_doc_target, $here_quote_character, $i,
6889 $saw_error );
6890}
6891
6892sub do_quote {
6893
6894 # follow (or continue following) quoted string(s)
6895 # $in_quote return code:
6896 # 0 - ok, found end
6897 # 1 - still must find end of quote whose target is $quote_character
6898 # 2 - still looking for end of first of two quotes
6899 #
6900 # Returns updated strings:
6901 # $quoted_string_1 = quoted string seen while in_quote=1
6902 # $quoted_string_2 = quoted string seen while in_quote=2
6903 my (
6904 $i, $in_quote, $quote_character,
6905 $quote_pos, $quote_depth, $quoted_string_1,
6906 $quoted_string_2, $rtokens, $rtoken_map,
6907 $max_token_index
6908 ) = @_;
6909
6910 my $in_quote_starting = $in_quote;
6911
6912 my $quoted_string;
6913 if ( $in_quote == 2 ) { # two quotes/quoted_string_1s to follow
6914 my $ibeg = $i;
6915 (
6916 $i, $in_quote, $quote_character, $quote_pos, $quote_depth,
6917 $quoted_string
6918 )
6919 = follow_quoted_string( $i, $in_quote, $rtokens, $quote_character,
6920 $quote_pos, $quote_depth, $max_token_index );
6921 $quoted_string_2 .= $quoted_string;
6922 if ( $in_quote == 1 ) {
6923 if ( $quote_character =~ /[\{\[\<\(]/ ) { $i++; }
6924 $quote_character = '';
6925 }
6926 else {
6927 $quoted_string_2 .= "\n";
6928 }
6929 }
6930
6931 if ( $in_quote == 1 ) { # one (more) quote to follow
6932 my $ibeg = $i;
6933 (
6934 $i, $in_quote, $quote_character, $quote_pos, $quote_depth,
6935 $quoted_string
6936 )
6937 = follow_quoted_string( $ibeg, $in_quote, $rtokens, $quote_character,
6938 $quote_pos, $quote_depth, $max_token_index );
6939 $quoted_string_1 .= $quoted_string;
6940 if ( $in_quote == 1 ) {
6941 $quoted_string_1 .= "\n";
6942 }
6943 }
6944 return ( $i, $in_quote, $quote_character, $quote_pos, $quote_depth,
6945 $quoted_string_1, $quoted_string_2 );
6946}
6947
6948sub follow_quoted_string {
6949
6950 # scan for a specific token, skipping escaped characters
6951 # if the quote character is blank, use the first non-blank character
6952 # input parameters:
6953 # $rtokens = reference to the array of tokens
6954 # $i = the token index of the first character to search
6955 # $in_quote = number of quoted strings being followed
6956 # $beginning_tok = the starting quote character
6957 # $quote_pos = index to check next for alphanumeric delimiter
6958 # output parameters:
6959 # $i = the token index of the ending quote character
6960 # $in_quote = decremented if found end, unchanged if not
6961 # $beginning_tok = the starting quote character
6962 # $quote_pos = index to check next for alphanumeric delimiter
6963 # $quote_depth = nesting depth, since delimiters '{ ( [ <' can be nested.
6964 # $quoted_string = the text of the quote (without quotation tokens)
6965 my ( $i_beg, $in_quote, $rtokens, $beginning_tok, $quote_pos, $quote_depth,
6966 $max_token_index )
6967 = @_;
6968 my ( $tok, $end_tok );
6969 my $i = $i_beg - 1;
6970 my $quoted_string = "";
6971
6972 TOKENIZER_DEBUG_FLAG_QUOTE && do {
6973 print STDOUT
6974"QUOTE entering with quote_pos = $quote_pos i=$i beginning_tok =$beginning_tok\n";
6975 };
6976
6977 # get the corresponding end token
6978 if ( $beginning_tok !~ /^\s*$/ ) {
6979 $end_tok = matching_end_token($beginning_tok);
6980 }
6981
6982 # a blank token means we must find and use the first non-blank one
6983 else {
6984 my $allow_quote_comments = ( $i < 0 ) ? 1 : 0; # i<0 means we saw a <cr>
6985
6986 while ( $i < $max_token_index ) {
6987 $tok = $rtokens->[ ++$i ];
6988
6989 if ( $tok !~ /^\s*$/ ) {
6990
6991 if ( ( $tok eq '#' ) && ($allow_quote_comments) ) {
6992 $i = $max_token_index;
6993 }
6994 else {
6995
6996 if ( length($tok) > 1 ) {
6997 if ( $quote_pos <= 0 ) { $quote_pos = 1 }
6998 $beginning_tok = substr( $tok, $quote_pos - 1, 1 );
6999 }
7000 else {
7001 $beginning_tok = $tok;
7002 $quote_pos = 0;
7003 }
7004 $end_tok = matching_end_token($beginning_tok);
7005 $quote_depth = 1;
7006 last;
7007 }
7008 }
7009 else {
7010 $allow_quote_comments = 1;
7011 }
7012 }
7013 }
7014
7015 # There are two different loops which search for the ending quote
7016 # character. In the rare case of an alphanumeric quote delimiter, we
7017 # have to look through alphanumeric tokens character-by-character, since
7018 # the pre-tokenization process combines multiple alphanumeric
7019 # characters, whereas for a non-alphanumeric delimiter, only tokens of
7020 # length 1 can match.
7021
7022 ###################################################################
7023 # Case 1 (rare): loop for case of alphanumeric quote delimiter..
7024 # "quote_pos" is the position the current word to begin searching
7025 ###################################################################
7026 if ( $beginning_tok =~ /\w/ ) {
7027
7028 # Note this because it is not recommended practice except
7029 # for obfuscated perl contests
7030 if ( $in_quote == 1 ) {
7031 write_logfile_entry(
7032 "Note: alphanumeric quote delimiter ($beginning_tok) \n");
7033 }
7034
7035 while ( $i < $max_token_index ) {
7036
7037 if ( $quote_pos == 0 || ( $i < 0 ) ) {
7038 $tok = $rtokens->[ ++$i ];
7039
7040 if ( $tok eq '\\' ) {
7041
7042 # retain backslash unless it hides the end token
7043 $quoted_string .= $tok
7044 unless $rtokens->[ $i + 1 ] eq $end_tok;
7045 $quote_pos++;
7046 last if ( $i >= $max_token_index );
7047 $tok = $rtokens->[ ++$i ];
7048 }
7049 }
7050 my $old_pos = $quote_pos;
7051
7052 unless ( defined($tok) && defined($end_tok) && defined($quote_pos) )
7053 {
7054
7055 }
7056 $quote_pos = 1 + index( $tok, $end_tok, $quote_pos );
7057
7058 if ( $quote_pos > 0 ) {
7059
7060 $quoted_string .=
7061 substr( $tok, $old_pos, $quote_pos - $old_pos - 1 );
7062
7063 $quote_depth--;
7064
7065 if ( $quote_depth == 0 ) {
7066 $in_quote--;
7067 last;
7068 }
7069 }
7070 else {
7071 $quoted_string .= substr( $tok, $old_pos );
7072 }
7073 }
7074 }
7075
7076 ########################################################################
7077 # Case 2 (normal): loop for case of a non-alphanumeric quote delimiter..
7078 ########################################################################
7079 else {
7080
7081 while ( $i < $max_token_index ) {
7082 $tok = $rtokens->[ ++$i ];
7083
7084 if ( $tok eq $end_tok ) {
7085 $quote_depth--;
7086
7087 if ( $quote_depth == 0 ) {
7088 $in_quote--;
7089 last;
7090 }
7091 }
7092 elsif ( $tok eq $beginning_tok ) {
7093 $quote_depth++;
7094 }
7095 elsif ( $tok eq '\\' ) {
7096
7097 # retain backslash unless it hides the beginning or end token
7098 $tok = $rtokens->[ ++$i ];
7099 $quoted_string .= '\\'
7100 unless ( $tok eq $end_tok || $tok eq $beginning_tok );
7101 }
7102 $quoted_string .= $tok;
7103 }
7104 }
7105 if ( $i > $max_token_index ) { $i = $max_token_index }
7106 return ( $i, $in_quote, $beginning_tok, $quote_pos, $quote_depth,
7107 $quoted_string );
7108}
7109
7110sub indicate_error {
7111 my ( $msg, $line_number, $input_line, $pos, $carrat ) = @_;
7112 interrupt_logfile();
7113 warning($msg);
7114 write_error_indicator_pair( $line_number, $input_line, $pos, $carrat );
7115 resume_logfile();
7116 return;
7117}
7118
7119sub write_error_indicator_pair {
7120 my ( $line_number, $input_line, $pos, $carrat ) = @_;
7121 my ( $offset, $numbered_line, $underline ) =
7122 make_numbered_line( $line_number, $input_line, $pos );
7123 $underline = write_on_underline( $underline, $pos - $offset, $carrat );
7124 warning( $numbered_line . "\n" );
7125 $underline =~ s/\s*$//;
7126 warning( $underline . "\n" );
7127 return;
7128}
7129
7130sub make_numbered_line {
7131
7132 # Given an input line, its line number, and a character position of
7133 # interest, create a string not longer than 80 characters of the form
7134 # $lineno: sub_string
7135 # such that the sub_string of $str contains the position of interest
7136 #
7137 # Here is an example of what we want, in this case we add trailing
7138 # '...' because the line is long.
7139 #
7140 # 2: (One of QAML 2.0's authors is a member of the World Wide Web Con ...
7141 #
7142 # Here is another example, this time in which we used leading '...'
7143 # because of excessive length:
7144 #
7145 # 2: ... er of the World Wide Web Consortium's
7146 #
7147 # input parameters are:
7148 # $lineno = line number
7149 # $str = the text of the line
7150 # $pos = position of interest (the error) : 0 = first character
7151 #
7152 # We return :
7153 # - $offset = an offset which corrects the position in case we only
7154 # display part of a line, such that $pos-$offset is the effective
7155 # position from the start of the displayed line.
7156 # - $numbered_line = the numbered line as above,
7157 # - $underline = a blank 'underline' which is all spaces with the same
7158 # number of characters as the numbered line.
7159
7160 my ( $lineno, $str, $pos ) = @_;
7161 my $offset = ( $pos < 60 ) ? 0 : $pos - 40;
7162 my $excess = length($str) - $offset - 68;
7163 my $numc = ( $excess > 0 ) ? 68 : undef;
7164
7165 if ( defined($numc) ) {
7166 if ( $offset == 0 ) {
7167 $str = substr( $str, $offset, $numc - 4 ) . " ...";
7168 }
7169 else {
7170 $str = "... " . substr( $str, $offset + 4, $numc - 4 ) . " ...";
7171 }
7172 }
7173 else {
7174
7175 if ( $offset == 0 ) {
7176 }
7177 else {
7178 $str = "... " . substr( $str, $offset + 4 );
7179 }
7180 }
7181
7182 my $numbered_line = sprintf( "%d: ", $lineno );
7183 $offset -= length($numbered_line);
7184 $numbered_line .= $str;
7185 my $underline = " " x length($numbered_line);
7186 return ( $offset, $numbered_line, $underline );
7187}
7188
7189sub write_on_underline {
7190
7191 # The "underline" is a string that shows where an error is; it starts
7192 # out as a string of blanks with the same length as the numbered line of
7193 # code above it, and we have to add marking to show where an error is.
7194 # In the example below, we want to write the string '--^' just below
7195 # the line of bad code:
7196 #
7197 # 2: (One of QAML 2.0's authors is a member of the World Wide Web Con ...
7198 # ---^
7199 # We are given the current underline string, plus a position and a
7200 # string to write on it.
7201 #
7202 # In the above example, there will be 2 calls to do this:
7203 # First call: $pos=19, pos_chr=^
7204 # Second call: $pos=16, pos_chr=---
7205 #
7206 # This is a trivial thing to do with substr, but there is some
7207 # checking to do.
7208
7209 my ( $underline, $pos, $pos_chr ) = @_;
7210
7211 # check for error..shouldn't happen
7212 unless ( ( $pos >= 0 ) && ( $pos <= length($underline) ) ) {
7213 return $underline;
7214 }
7215 my $excess = length($pos_chr) + $pos - length($underline);
7216 if ( $excess > 0 ) {
7217 $pos_chr = substr( $pos_chr, 0, length($pos_chr) - $excess );
7218 }
7219 substr( $underline, $pos, length($pos_chr) ) = $pos_chr;
7220 return ($underline);
7221}
7222
7223sub pre_tokenize {
7224
7225 # Break a string, $str, into a sequence of preliminary tokens. We
7226 # are interested in these types of tokens:
7227 # words (type='w'), example: 'max_tokens_wanted'
7228 # digits (type = 'd'), example: '0755'
7229 # whitespace (type = 'b'), example: ' '
7230 # any other single character (i.e. punct; type = the character itself).
7231 # We cannot do better than this yet because we might be in a quoted
7232 # string or pattern. Caller sets $max_tokens_wanted to 0 to get all
7233 # tokens.
7234 my ( $str, $max_tokens_wanted ) = @_;
7235
7236 # we return references to these 3 arrays:
7237 my @tokens = (); # array of the tokens themselves
7238 my @token_map = (0); # string position of start of each token
7239 my @type = (); # 'b'=whitespace, 'd'=digits, 'w'=alpha, or punct
7240
7241 do {
7242
7243 # whitespace
7244 if ( $str =~ /\G(\s+)/gc ) { push @type, 'b'; }
7245
7246 # numbers
7247 # note that this must come before words!
7248 elsif ( $str =~ /\G(\d+)/gc ) { push @type, 'd'; }
7249
7250 # words
7251 elsif ( $str =~ /\G(\w+)/gc ) { push @type, 'w'; }
7252
7253 # single-character punctuation
7254 elsif ( $str =~ /\G(\W)/gc ) { push @type, $1; }
7255
7256 # that's all..
7257 else {
7258 return ( \@tokens, \@token_map, \@type );
7259 }
7260
7261 push @tokens, $1;
7262 push @token_map, pos($str);
7263
7264 } while ( --$max_tokens_wanted != 0 );
7265
7266 return ( \@tokens, \@token_map, \@type );
7267}
